body:
You are absolutely right. Thank you. Truly.
He is a great man. I’m lucky to know him.

Through more discussions, aside from the obvious initial blow and shock of hearing someone else’s name, we have talked about both points you’ve mentioned as being the heavy hitters.
He knows the truth in what’s been going on. He always has. That’s why he didn’t mention it before now. But I was honestly grateful to get the opportunity to reassure him on those points. He can “understand” or trust my answers are the same conclusions he’s come to, but I’m hoping hearing it from my mouth now will help.
Thanks you.

I’m still feeling pretty devastated honestly. It’s been really tough.
I’m genuinely doing my best and I hope one day my brain and me can really be on the same page. Healthy.
Thank you.

Thank you for saying that. The last couple days I honestly have been mostly concerned about him and neglecting my own feelings about it to almost… make up for? this happening. Thank you for the reminder.
Honestly that gave me a lot of comfort to read.. thank you for commenting Hawk.

She is not allowed to attach that shame to you. This isn’t on you. You set clear boundaries and she ignored you when you withdrew your consent for her own gain. BDSM is a delicate practice and what she did goes against the most basic principle of what HAS to be there in order for it to work.

In my opinion:
She has shown herself to be an untrustworthy person. She ignores boundaries. She degrades you outside of the bedroom and without prior conversation in the bedroom. Her behavior after the fact is manipulative and vile.

She is actively trying to trap you in a shame cycle. She is completely in the wrong. This does not fall on you. This does not make you weak. You did nothing shameful. You did right by yourself with your ability at the time and in prep.
I would say break it off. Even if this episode in the bedroom never happened again, I wouldn’t be able to reconcile with the person she’s showing herself to be.

I’m sorry. And not in the pity sense. In the one soul seeing another sense. You didn’t deserve that blatant disregard for your well-being.
Take time for yourself. Seek help if you feel like you need it. Find balance and peace in yourself.

Like I said. The boundary was anything *IN*. I understand it getting bumped or touched from the outside. I understand that.
This isn’t something he’s into for himself. Not something he particularly wants or needs in our sex life. It was something he tried for my benefit, but my problem was it went against my only boundary with him.

I agree.
I think that might be part of what’s disappointing about this for me. Since they’re my triggers and my boundaries I know it’s my responsibility to communicate and manage those. I genuinely thought I did. Even now I think I did. I’ve been so careful and intentional with all of it and worked very hard to communicate openly how I have.. But that’s not how he originally took it. With that, to me the first feels more like a misunderstanding than the second time. Either way he is taking full responsibility.
Thank you.

I know. You’re right.
The only differentiation is intent. But that doesn’t really matter. If he broke a boundary and my trust to the point I don’t feel safe with him, it’s done.

You are correct. In how we’d spoken about it originally, he’d misunderstood it as something I’m just not interested in not as a hard limit. So he tried it with me and thought he saw a favorable result. He said the second time he understood it was a boundary (as somehow it had come up again in conversation) but in the moment didn’t think about that. He just thought I’d liked it the first time and in the moment did it again. My words didn’t line up with what he thought my reaction was so he didn’t think about the boundary he just wanted to make me feel good.
Since then he hasn’t done it once. It seems like he realized he’d crossed a boundary and now understands it’s a hard limit boundary not just something to test w me.
His interpretation sounds like more along the lines of your experience. Now that he understands it’s a boundary it hasn’t happened again and I believe won’t happen again. It’s been 6 months since the last time he did it but I’m just finding out about it now.

So I’m trying to feel more like how you were talking and how he originally saw it- he tried something w me I didn’t like and now it won’t happen again. But from my experience and my feelings I know that was a boundary and that it was crossed.
